# ilabhu

> Open-source, self-hostable certification exam simulator (CKA, CKAD, CKS, RHCSA, ...). Provisions full exam environments — multi-domain, time-bounded, scored — in the user's own AWS / GCP / Azure / DigitalOcean account, or on Linux servers the user already operates.

ilabhu is licensed Apache 2.0 and distributed as source under [github.com/eltonlaice/ilabhu](https://github.com/eltonlaice/ilabhu). It is **not** a SaaS product — every operator runs their own control plane and pays their own infrastructure (or pays nothing, with the BYO-hosts adapter).

## How it works

An exam is a versioned directory under `exams/` containing:

- `exam.yaml` — manifest with weighted domains, ~15–20 tasks, declared infrastructure providers, time limit, passing score.
- One Terraform module per supported cloud provider (or a `setup.sh` / `teardown.sh` pair for the BYO-hosts adapter).

When a user starts a session, the control plane (`ilabhud`, written in Go) picks the chosen provider's adapter, provisions the environment in the user's account or hosts, fetches the kubeconfig, and exposes per-task `validate` endpoints that drive `kubectl` / `shell` / `http` checks.

## Providers (all shipped)

| Provider | Auth | Cost per 2h session |
|---|---|---|
| AWS | `sts:AssumeRole` + external id | ~$0.05 |
| DigitalOcean | Personal Access Token | ~$0.04 |
| GCP | Service Account key JSON | ~$0.04 |
| Azure | Service Principal + client secret | ~$0.08 |
| BYO-hosts | SSH private key + host list | $0 |

## Validator kinds

- `kubectl` — runs `kubectl` against the session's kubeconfig; matches stdout via `expect_equals` / `expect_contains` / `expect_exit_code`.
- `shell` — pipes a script over SSH to `/bin/sh` on the access host; same expectation matchers as `kubectl`.
- `http` — `GET` against a URL; supports `{{public_ip}}` substitution; checks `expect_status` / `expect_body_contains`.

## Repository structure

- `control-plane/` — Go daemon `ilabhud`; HTTP API at `/v1/exams`, `/v1/sessions`, `/v1/sessions/{id}/tasks/{task_id}/validate`.
- `web/` — Next.js 16 (App Router) frontend.
- `exams/<exam-code>/<slug>/` — exam manifests + provider modules.
- `docs/` — `architecture.md`, `exam-schema.md` (+ JSON Schema), `authoring-an-exam.md`, `byo-cloud-setup.md`, `troubleshooting.md`.
- `site/` — this landing page, deployed to https://ilabhu.com/ via GitHub Pages.

## What ilabhu is not

- Not a shared sandbox. Every session lives in resources the user owns.
- Not a chat tutor. There is no LLM that grades free-form answers; validations are deterministic shell / kubectl / http checks.
- Not a SaaS. There is no `https://app.ilabhu.com`. The landing page is a brochure; the product is the daemon you self-host.
- Not a CKA cram course. ilabhu provides the environment and the grading; you bring the study.
